title: AI 디자인 시스템의 헬베티카를 꿈꾸며
content: AI와 함께 프로덕트를 만들면 최소한의 기능을 구현하는 일이 훨씬 쉬워집니다. 원하는 것을 설명하고 몇 번 수정하면 어느 정도 사용할 수 있는 화면이 만들어집니다. 하지만 기능이 작동하는 것과 좋은 UX를 제공하는 것은 다릅니다. 평균 이상의 경험을 만들려면 결과를 계속 확인하고 세부적인 부분을 다듬어야 합니다. 그러다 보면 신경 써야 할 것이 많아집니다.

title: VPC
content: 들어가며 최근 웹 서비스, 클라우드, 그리고 AI 애플리케이션 개발에서 인프라 구조를 이해하는 일은 점점 더 중요해지고 있습니다. 예전에는 서버 한 대에 웹 서버와 데이터베이스를 함께 올려 운영하는 경우도 많았지만, 요즘은 서비스 규모가 커지고 구조가 복잡해지면서 네트워크 설계 역시 중요한 요소가 되었습니다. AWS를 사용하다 보면 EC2, RDS, Load Balancer, NAT Gateway 같은 여러 서비스를 만나게 됩니다. 그리고 이 서비스들을 구성할 때 거의 항상 함께 등장하는 개념이 있습니다. 바로 VPC입니다. 처음에는 VPC라는 용어가 낯설 수 있습니다. Virtual Private Cloud라는 이름도 어렵게 느껴지고, Subnet, CIDR, Route Table, Internet Gateway, Security Group 같은 용어들이 한꺼번에 나오기 때문에 더 헷갈릴 수 있습니다. 하지만 VPC는 어렵게만 볼 개념은 아닙니다. 조금 쉽게 말하면, VPC는 클라우드 안에 만드는 우리 서비스만의…

title: David Rudnick on the “borderline impossible” process of designing a bespoke blackletter typeface for Arsenal
content: For the past four years, the designer has been building a hand-drawn, three-weight type family that pays homage to one of the most beloved players in Arsenal’s history: David Rocastle. Here, It’s Nice That sits down with David and Arsenal Creative Studio lead Johnnie Campbell to get behind the scenes of the mammoth project.

title: Design with abandon! Núria Balinha’s zines are the result of working without inhibitions
content: For the designer, “thinking too much” is just another way of making work that feels “forced or silly”.

title: Can motion design have a “body language”? Studio Kiln thinks so
content: Studio Kiln are behind motion design for MTV, Vinted, Netflix and even the Baftas, so that’s why Charlie Hockling and Nathan Smith joined our Nicer Tuesdays stage to take the audience behind the golden mask to learn how a brand can “have a body language” and craft, elegance and magic can be felt through expressive motion design.Special thanks to EartH (Evolutionary Arts Hackney).

title: “Less bank, more life”: Barkas gives Nigerian digital bank Kuda an identity with the pace of Lagos
content: Spanning chunky geometric letterforms, a custom Naira sign and hand-drawn illustrations, the new brand moves Kuda on from its challenger days.

title: “I’m merely cosplaying as a type designer”: Raoul Gottschling on chasing ridiculous ‘what if’ questions
content: The Berlin-based designer talks to us about imposter syndrome, being self taught and the creative process behind his portfolio of imaginative, playful and robust fonts.

title: Mucho reaches beyond Silicon Valley with the branding for Biotic, the organisation behind breakthrough biology
content: Boundary-pushing science is often difficult to understand, that’s where clear and accessible brand design often comes in to help. With the promising results from SpudCells, branding agency Mucho has stepped in to introduce innovation to the public.

title: How Nomad named and branded six rugby sevens clubs with no home city — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: Ultimate Sevens is a rugby sevens league – backed by BIA Sports Group, the owners of Premier League football club Sunderland – whose first season took place in Cardiff, Biarritz and London in September 2026. It needed six club identities for that season, which were all created by London-based design studio Nomad. “We had six weeks to do it – to name them, the themes, and design them, and get them trademarked,” explains Co-founder & Executive Creative Director Stu Watson.

title: SMLXL’s identity for MoMA PS1’s Warm Up has letters that dance to music — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: Warm Up, MoMA PS1’s summer festival, has brought together music, art and community in New York for nearly three decades, with past line-ups including Arca, SOPHIE, Solange, Jamie xx, Four Tet and Grimes. Its 28th edition fell in the institution’s 50th anniversary year, with a line-up centred on experimental music. Ahead of its 24th July - 28th August 2026 run, New York and Barcelona-based design company SMLXL came on board to create Warm Up’s musical identity and campaign.

title: Frequency leads LOTIPA and ImaginaryFriend’s identity for a DJ’s matcha — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: Matchalita is a brand of high-grade ceremonial matcha, founded by DJ and artist Carlita. US-based creative company ImaginaryFriend came on board to lead the creative direction for its identity, while Brazil and Portugal-based design studio LOTIPA developed the graphic design system, extending it into motion. “There wasn’t really a moment where ‘our bit’ ended and ‘their bit’ began,” ImaginaryFriend’s Co-Chief Creative Officer Dave Brown tells us.

title: Why Carolanebel Studio turned a fleur-de-lys into a bird for Club Pays — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: Club Pays is a café on Montréal’s Plaza Saint-Hubert that becomes a room for shows, open mics, reading circles and talks in the evening. It is run by OUI Québec, a non-partisan umbrella organisation for the Québec independence movement, and its model comes from the casals of Catalonia and the herriko tabernas of the Basque Country – citizen-run bars that work as meeting places, mobilisation centres and fundraisers. Surpluses from Club Pays’ coffee, beer and events go back into the movement.

title: How Studio Dial turns tactile generative experiments into brand tools — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: Studio Dial bridges physical craft and digital tools to make identities, campaigns and experimental websites, working as a small, collaborative team that treats code as a tactile medium. The London-based practice draws on both sides of founder Natalia Witwicka’s experience, including branding at Pentagram and global AI campaigns with Google Creative Lab and DeepMind. In this interview, we talk about how freelancing led to starting the studio faster than she anticipated, how the team lets mistakes bring a human qua…

title: Why Field of Practice treats branding as a practice of change — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: Field of Practice’s Co-founders Kristin Lueke and Nermin Moufti treat branding as a question of who is not in the room when the decisions get made. “Design is never neutral,” they tell us, so a brand that states values has to pay for them in how the business runs. The women and member-owned strategic design studio that they run from Chicago and New Mexico was taking on clients by January 2021, before it even had a name or a bank account. They built it to test whether two people could make a living on a four-day we…

title: The idea of home shapes Base Design’s identity for Ray’s Waterfront — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: Ray’s Waterfront is a family-run restaurant and bar on the Small Boat Harbor on Resurrection Bay, in Seward, Alaska – a town of fewer than 3,000 people. Ray Simutis, a former New York taxi driver turned commercial fisherman, and Leslie Simutis, a trained cook, opened it in 1988, Ray working the bar and Leslie the kitchen. After both passed, the restaurant passed to their daughters, Anna and Janina.

title: How Sunny Side Up drew from David Carson’s editorial chaos to craft Co-Museum’s dynamic identity — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: Co-Museum is aiming to redefine the art landscape by offering asset-backed collectibles, where buyers purchase fractional ownership in underlying cultural assets. For Singapore-based brand agency Sunny Side Up, this mission to make art more inclusive and community-driven demanded a visual approach that would challenge traditional museum aesthetics while honouring the tactile nature of cultural heritage.

title: PARTERRE subdued identity for Max Manavi-Huber reflects the humanity and technicality in his work — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: “The colour palette is inspired by Max’s photographs,” Kevin Nowak, Creative Director of Vienna-based design studio PARTERRE tells us, recounting the thought process behind their identity for Vienesse photographer Max Manavi-Huber. “A lot of his photos are shot outside in nature,” Nowak continues, “so it was clear to use an earthy colour palette, and grey, brown uncoated papers for the stationary,” allowing the photographs themselves to take centre stage.

title: Concrete poetry, history, and a Scottish wildflower blue collide in Warriors Studio’s brand for BARD — The Brand Identity – Home of the Greatest in Graphic & Brand Design
content: BARD is an award-winning architecture practice that has built its vision on the legacy of Scottish architect, designer, and artist Charles Rennie Mackintosh, and are the only architects entrusted with building on Mackintosh’s oeuvre with their work at Grade A-listed building Windyhill.

title: Nobody wants your AI app
content: The switchboard operator’s job was automated out of existence. The work it became, the invisible systems that now connect every call, is worth more than the job ever was. AI is about to do the same thing to the app. The people buying AI are blunt about the fact that the future is intelligence that disappears into existing platforms. Everyone wants it invisible and under their total control at the same time. We are all racing to build AI apps that nobody wants to open. Specifically, the standalone AI app, the thing…

title: What I told the CFO when he asked why design matters
content: How to sell design and show the impact of design outcomes to business and finance leaders. Many years ago a business unit CFO told me: “I don’t need another presentation explaining why design is important. I need to know whether investing another million dollars in design will outperform investing it in engineering or marketing.” That conversation changed how I talk about design. title: Taste is not a design methodology
content: Judgment brings the facts. Agency puts them on the table. AI assisted. It has become our favorite answer to AI-generated sameness. The reality is good products come from judgment built on facts, and the agency to use them when the room prefers opinions. Ask Rick Rubin what he does and he’ll tell you he has “no technical ability” and knows nothing about music. title: Secret agent bot: accessibility matters for the agents even if you can’t see them
content: Two readers, one page. The agent never sees the surface you designed; it reads the structure underneath. AI assisted. The semantic structure screen readers have used for decades now also decide whether ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, and Perplexity can read your page at all. In 2016 I had a series of calls with the federal government’s top accessibility expert as the leader of a design team, and I learned more in those conversations than in years of reading specifications.
